target_customer: Unbanked and underbanked consumers in Mexico
problem: Many Mexicans lack bank accounts; Flinto let them send money, pay merchants and bills from a phone, depositing cash at local shops.
business_model: Digital wallet with fees on payments and cash deposits

founders.name: Tiago Sada
founders.background_notes: Later joined Tools for Humanity per YC bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile wallet with cash in via retail networks, bill payments and compliance; standard fintech engineering with integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Retail cash-in partnerships help but wallets in Mexico were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Merged with Grow Mobility in June 2019; the Flinto brand was to be phased out.

market_need_then: Over a third of Mexicans were unbanked per later fintech coverage; Grin's cofounder said a wallet was needed to reach Latin America's underbanked.

rebrands.why: TechCrunch says the Flinto brand would be phased out over time

brand_strength.rationale: A 2018 Expansion article spelled it 'Flint', suggesting weak recall; the brand was phased out after the 2019 merger. Not to be confused with the Flinto prototyping app.

outcome_analysis: Flinto raised a small $1.5M pre-seed in June 2018 after YC, then merged with the scooter company Grow Mobility in June 2019, which wanted a wallet for the underbanked. The brand was to be retired. Grow Mobility later retrenched across Latin America, so the wallet's long-run outcome is unclear; the soft landing label is an inference since sources do not describe terms.
notes: flinto.app returned 503, so the site could not be checked. A first pass confused this company with the unrelated Flinto prototyping app; the YC page shows this is the Mexico wallet. The round amount comes from the YC page listing (opened) and Expansion headline via search; investors not confirmed (CB Insights lists Sinai Ventures, Mexamerica Ventures, YC; unverified). Expansion named different founders (Carlos Sanchez, Paolo D'Amico) and spelled Flint; unresolved. YC says acquired by Grin; TechCrunch says merged with Grow Mobility. No dated 2018 competitor sources found.
